pr_title: [api-minor] XFA - Support text search in XFA documents.
pr_body:
Moves the logic out of TextLayerBuilder to handle
highlighting matches into a new separate class `TextHighlighter`
that can be used with regular PDFs and XFA PDFs.

To mimic the current find functionality in XFA, two arrays
from the XFA rendering are created to get the text content
and map those to DOM nodes.

Fixes #13878

issue_context.title: XFA - Searching a text is broken
issue_context.body: Since the rendering is done thanks to HTML we should likely use the "normal" firefox search feature (at least for the builtin viewer)
comments:
A few quick observations/questions:
 - How would you then prevent searching from matching strings in the UI (toolbar labels, outline items, and so on), if we simply use the "normal" browser search for XFA documents?
 - How would this work for XFA Foreground documents, which may potentially require both a `textLayer` *and* a `xfaLayer`?
 - Given that pages are lazily loaded and removed once out of view (for memory/performance reasons), using a "normal" browser search wouldn't really help for pages not actually visible!
   (This is a large part of the reason for having a *custom* find-implementation in the first place, even for regular PDF documents, since all `textLayer`s cannot be assumed to be visible or even exist.)

>     * How would this work for XFA Foreground documents, which may potentially require both a `textLayer` _and_ a `xfaLayer`

Looking at the spec, XFAF documents are are only suppose to use form controls (section `Grammar Excluded from XFAF`), so for this case we would do a regular search with the text layer.

review_comments: Missing an `and` at the start of this line?
A static method can directly call another static method, hence `this.shouldBuildText` ought to work.
That was failing with lint, but seems to be fine now that I upgraded
I take that back, it fails because `this` doesn't exist because we're in the closure.
Sorry, didn't notice the closure; please disregard my comment :-)
Similar to the comment above, for the `enable`-method, but for the `!this.enabled` case instead.
We currently call disable without enabling since we cancel things out before starting. Since this is safe to call without enabling, I think we should just leave it as is.
Maybe just add a `if (!this.enabled) { return; }` at the top then, since none of the code in this method needs to run if it's already disabled?

Please remember to also update https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/a936509b77ae4f7e49dea57cf2e2a0aacd062516/web/text_layer_builder.js#L440-L446 and https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/master/web/interfaces.js accordingly,

Should we throw an Error if `this.enabled` here, or at the very least print a warning and return early, since multiple `enable`-calls (without `disable` between) seem like a bug elsewhere in the code-base?

I'm not finding an corresponding `disable` call, for the xfaLayer-case, anywhere!?

Please note that the xfaLayer, similar to the textLayer, will now be removed from the DOM when the page becomes inactive (to reduce memory usage and improve performance).
Hence it seems to me that you'd want to, in the `cancelRendering`-method, ensure that you also *disable* the textHighlighter for the xfaLayer-case to properly clean-up here.
